Section 6: Detailed Accounting of Covered Entity's Expenditures from 340B Profits
Programs or Services funded/purchased with 340B funds:

During calendar year 2025, Lorain County Health & Dentistry (LCH&D) provided approximately 4,100 patient encounters for 2,047 uninsured patients. In accordance with our Board-approved Sliding Fee Discount Program and HRSA requirements, LCH&D adjusted $978,583.33 in patient fees for these uninsured encounters. These adjustments represent the difference between the full charges for services provided and the reduced amounts patients were responsible for paying based on their eligibility under the Sliding Fee Discount Program. A total of $420,531.47 in 340B program savings was used to offset a portion of these discounted services, helping ensure uninsured patients continued to receive access to comprehensive medical, behavioral health, dental, OB/GYN, and vision services regardless of their ability to pay. The remaining cost of these fee adjustments was supported through other organizational resources.
Other uses of 340B funds not otherwise listed above:

Lorain County Health & Dentistry (LCH&D), a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), is committed to serving the underserved and uninsured residents of Lorain County by providing comprehensive, high-quality healthcare regardless of a patient's ability to pay. Our integrated services include primary medical care, behavioral health, dental care, obstetrics and gynecology (OB/GYN), and vision services. The 340B Drug Pricing Program plays a vital role in supporting our mission by allowing us to stretch limited resources and reinvest savings into patient care and expanded access to services. In 2025, we expanded our pharmacy services by opening a second in-house pharmacy, improving access to affordable medications for our patients. We also provide a mail-order pharmacy service to ensure patients who face transportation or other barriers can conveniently receive their medications. During 2025, LCH&D served 17,588 unique patients through 58,005 patient visits. Of those, 2,047 patients were uninsured and accounted for approximately 4,100 patient encounters. These uninsured patients were offered services under our Sliding Fee Discount Program based on their household income and ability to pay. Savings generated through the 340B Program helped offset the cost of providing care to these patients, allowing us to continue delivering essential healthcare services while maintaining financial sustainability. It is also important to note that a portion of the prescriptions reported as "cash" sales reflects situations where patients elected to purchase medications at our discounted cash price because it was less expensive than using their insurance benefits. This commonly occurs when a patient's insurance deductible or out-of-pocket cost is significantly higher than our pharmacy's cash price (for example, a $250 copayment or deductible). These transactions are recorded as cash sales, making them difficult to separately quantify, but they represent an important way the 340B Program helps reduce medication costs for our patients.

LCH&D does not administer 340B-purchased drugs. All medications administered within our clinics are non-340B drugs.
